clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-month-old male presented with pruritic skin rashes spreading initially on hands and feet then generalized with follicular papules and desquamative exanthem. Dermatologist evaluation on hospital day 7 documented diffuse erythematosquamous plaques, follicular hyperkeratosis, palmoplantar keratoderma with spared areas, and clinically diagnosed generalized papulodescamative disease compatible with pityriasis rubra pilaris. Clinical progression showed slight improvement and persistent erythematous lesions at 14 days, with eventual complete resolution at 3 months. Histopathology was ordered but not reported. Treatment and additional rule-out evidence were not specified.
